neighbours.label: the comma (or the next 'the') that closes a fronted introductory phrase, just before the main clause starts
fire: To raise money for the trip, the students sold cookies after school.
Hoping to find shelter, the hikers walked toward the distant lights.
Tired of waiting, the old man left the office without a word.
In his long career as a judge, he never once lost his temper.
Looking for a cheaper flat, Maria moved to the edge of town.
Surprised, the cat jumped off the table and ran outside.
To protect the crops from frost, the farmers lit small fires.
After hearing the forecast, the captain kept the boat in port.
quiet: The students sold cookies after school to raise money for the trip.
The hikers walked toward the distant lights hoping to find shelter.
The old man left the office without a word because he was tired.
He never once lost his temper in his long career as a judge.
Maria moved to the edge of town to find a cheaper flat.
The cat jumped off the table and ran outside in surprise.
The farmers lit small fires to protect the crops from frost.
The captain kept the boat in port after hearing the forecast.
